scope: Cross-family findings from cards measured in this campaign. Every entry cites the card and the native/timing evidence; none of them is a direction ban.

append_after_L7.claim: Package results are not predictable from their members; every package must be measured
evidence: pkg-vit-16pass: members n11 +0.0386 (NS) and n11b -0.0536 (NS) -> package +0.0096ms FASTER_95 (CI [0.0028,0.0164])
pkg-f05-mbatch: members n05c +0.0315 (NS) and n05d -0.0073 (NS) -> package +0.0013ms INDISTINCT
pkg-f04-26pass: members n03 -0.0234 (NS) and n03b +0.0485 (NS) -> package -0.0404ms SLOWER_95
n12b-f14-scale is itself a two-mechanism package on 8 PASS -> -0.0009ms INDISTINCT with a tight CI
append_after_L7.consequence: Never add single-point savings to predict a package, and never reject a mechanism because its single point was INDISTINCT: build the package and measure it once, with an ablation arm when a member's own point estimate was negative.

append_after_L7.claim: Budget before implementation keeps register-hungry variants out of the build queue
evidence: n05c: 12-acc full M doubling needs ~119-138 GRF > 128 -> rejected before coding; D2 (Q/K 8 acc + V 4 acc, peak 102) implemented, native matched the budget exactly (weights 104->56, A 128->256, dpas 128, max_r 127)
n05d: same for C64 (D1 133-137 rejected, D2 101 implemented; native weights 56->32, A 64->128)
n03b: budget showed 12 acc is reachable but the kernel already sits at max_r=127, so the only failure modes were scratch>0 or IGC serialisation
append_after_L7.consequence: Each memory-layout card should deliver a BUDGET.md first; a rejected budget with a named missing proof is a valid card outcome.

append_after_L7.claim: A card's premise can be stale; verifying it is part of the work
evidence: n06b: the card assumed F06 C64 still had 2 accumulators and could halve weight loads again; the parent was already at 4 acc with 2 DPAS per weight tile, so the card pivoted to the A tile (the only tile still at 2x reuse) and delivered +0.018ms
n03b: the card assumed 6 accumulators; the live kernel has 8
append_after_L7.consequence: Read the parent's ISA before accepting the card's premise; when the premise fails, pivot to the nearest real axis and record why.

append_after_L7.claim: Byte accounting must use the runtime active mask, not the static lane width
evidence: n18 estimated 602.9 MB of gathers with 301.5 MB duplicate for F01; n18b proved the whole entry block is one divergent region (cmp lane,16 -> goto) so only lanes 0..15 execute, each gather carries 64 B: real traffic 301.40 MB and duplicate 0 B

n18b also proved the mask is active by contradiction: the shK write address (q<<8)+(lane<<4) is not clamped, so a 32-lane execution would overwrite the next subgroup token block, yet the SPV passes both gold frames
append_after_L7.consequence: Before pricing any duplicate-read or dedup candidate, check the enclosing mask/branch on the captured ISA. A static 32-lane formula can double the apparent traffic and invent a duplicate stream that does not exist.

append_after_L7.claim: Isolated per-PASS time does not predict whole-frame sensitivity; what matters is whether the removed work is on the critical path or already hidden by concurrency
evidence: F20 (ord 230) is the largest isolated dispatch at 1.367 ms (7.5%) and its profile is 73% fragment-transport messages, yet deleting 32 then 64 of those messages (Q, Y, Q+Y) moved the frame by +0.0257 / -0.0181 / +0.0115 ms, all INDISTINCT: the messages are already hidden by other resident workgroups
F01 (ord 0) is the second largest at 1.164 ms (6.4%) and deleting a scalar modulo chain (7168->6519 instructions, no message change) delivered +0.0791 ms FASTER_95 6/6
F09 (2.8% only) delivered +0.171 ms by deleting a shared-memory roundtrip plus one workgroup barrier
append_after_L7.consequence: Rank candidates by the kind of work removed (barriers, serialised scalar chains, cross-owner roundtrips that sit on the critical path) and not by the dispatch size alone; a message-count drop inside a concurrent kernel can be entirely hidden.

append_after_L7.claim: Within-batch CI understates between-batch drift; a difference below ~0.03 ms can flip sign between two balanced batches
evidence: abl-small-steps batch: 9-step head vs the same head with n06+pkg-vit+n06b reverted gave saving(head-ablation) = -0.031750 CI[-0.0458,-0.0177], i.e. the reversion looked 0.0318 ms faster
confirm3 batch (fresh, balanced ABC, same two plans): A-C 0.860012 CI[0.8407,0.8793], A-B 0.884494 CI[0.8732,0.8958] => B-C = -0.024482 CI[-0.0377,-0.0112], i.e. the reversion is 0.0245 ms SLOWER
both batches had CI half-widths of 0.007-0.014 and 6/6 consistent pairs, yet they disagree in sign
append_after_L7.consequence: Treat any delta below ~0.03 ms as unresolved unless it replicates in a second balanced batch; do not adopt an ablation (or any marginal step) on one batch. Prefer the configuration with fewer changes when the effect is unresolved, and record the disagreement instead of the winning number.

append_after_L7.claim: Widening a cooperative-matrix fragment in SPIR-V does not make the driver emit wider memory messages
evidence: n02d replaced eight (8,16) bias loads with two (8,64) band loads: SPIR-V types did change ((8,16,ACC) 8->0, (8,64,ACC) 0->2), the fixed and fb2 gold frames still matched, yet ISA kept 64 load.ugm.d32x16t and added 21 more send messages (597->618, +149 static instructions)
the loads still carry the same bytes; only the source-level fragment shape changed
append_after_L7.consequence: Judge a fragment-shape change by the ISA message mix, not by the SPIR-V type. If load.ugm.d32x16t does not fall, the driver re-narrowed and the candidate is A-class regardless of the SPIR-V.

append_after_L7.claim: F18 contract has 4x duplicated A and weight reads but the removal is blocked by the register ceiling, not by the algorithm
evidence: n20 measured per WG: A (gM) rows 64 KiB where dedup would be 16 KiB (4x), weights 128 KiB where dedup would be 32 KiB (4x); seed and Y are 1x; the segment has no SLM (Workgroup Memory 0, send.slm 0) and no global write->read, so there is no arena or roundtrip to delete
the only shape that halves both messages and bytes (8 accumulators, weight 4x->1x) needs +32 GRF, but the kernel already uses r124 of 128 and scratch 0 -> it must spill
the shape that keeps 4 accumulators (2mx2n -> 1mx4n) halves the A messages (2048->1024, -15% static) but raises weight bytes 128->256 KiB and total bytes by +43%, so it is a trade, not a deletion
append_after_L7.consequence: Record F18 contract as structurally infeasible on this identity and register budget. Any future proposal that removes the 4x redundancy must first answer where the registers come from (currently r124/104, scratch 0).

append_after_L7.claim: The narrow-read/address axis of this network is exhausted: 21 families audited, zero sites worth a card
evidence: n15 resolved current-identity ISA for all 232 ordinals by baseline_kernel_hash (the recorded NATIVE-INDEX paths were stale for F04/F05/F06/F10) and tallied 7,741 narrow messages, 33,013 half-width register moves and 107,643 ugm sends

only two sites could be widened (F20 [100F0..10130] 3 messages, F21 [4458..44C0] 6 messages) and both are priced out: F20 needs 3 extra movs to merge non-contiguous data registers (net zero, and L12 measured the same kernel insensitive to 32/64 message deletions), F21 has an unresolved per-lane step
no place in the whole network does shl 16 + or/and 0xFFFF half packing (16 such shifts checked individually), and only 0.76% of sends carry immediates, so the short-lived-base axis is also empty
append_after_L7.consequence: Do not open narrow-read or address-formation cards. Any future site must show a countable message or instruction deletion that is not offset by added register moves.

append_after_L7.claim: The gated debug path is neither a frame cost nor a register reservoir
evidence: n21 removed the entire if(debug) path from the F18 C128 contract kernel: static instructions 1947->1720 (-227, 11.7%), non-issuing send entries 429->364, store.ugm 128->64
the frame did not move (+0.005059 ms, CI[-0.0104,+0.0205]) so instruction fetch of never-executed code is not a bottleneck
the data-side register peak fell only 124->114 (a whole band r118/r120/r122/r124 disappeared) while max_r_any stayed 127; scratch unchanged. 10 registers, not the 32 F18s M4 needs
the dead path owns no dedicated registers (it only touches r1..r96); it extends the live range of the f16 staging r12..r15 and thereby pushes the high band up by 10
append_after_L7.consequence: Do not count debug-path removal as a gain and do not use it to unlock register-hungry shapes; dead code only returns the width it inflates in others. Remaining headroom after the strip is 14 GRF (114/128), so a 6-acc form needing +16 still misses by 2. The register ceiling has to be answered by fewer live accumulators/fragments or by a shape change.

append_after_L7.claim: Source-level redundant subgroup operations may already be folded by the driver; the parent ISA is the only authority on whether a repack costs anything
evidence: n22 found the F15 P->PV join requesting 24 subgroup operations per call where 16 are provable bitwise identities and 4 are duplicates
a census of the parent ISA showed only 70 indirect moves (2x35 shuffles) with 35 = 4x8 join + 2 den + 1 epilogue and zero residual, i.e. the join already costs its theoretical minimum of 4

rewriting the source to the minimal 4 changed nothing at the native level: indirect moves stayed 70, a0 references 395, dpas 64, send 476 (static instructions fell 3692->3520 from unrelated scaffolding)
append_after_L7.consequence: Before pricing a source-level redundancy, count the corresponding native operations; if they already equal the lower bound, the card is BLOCKED at the source layer and no GPU time is warranted. Same family of mistake as L11 (static lane width) and L14 (fragment shape).

append_after_L7.claim: Cross-PASS layout folding works mechanically (both sides land) but the single site measured is sub-floor
evidence: n24 folded the F18 body->contract gM layout: consumer A reads 256 d32x8t -> 0 with d32x64t 8->40, consumer static instructions 1947->1193 (-38.7%), producer stores 160->144 plus 2 wide stores, dpas unchanged, four independent proofs incl. an exhaustive element-equivalence check

the frame did not respond: +0.009774 ms CI[-0.0117,+0.0313]. The consumer segment is only ~0.021 ms isolated (2.4% of the frame), so a 38.7% instruction cut there is ~0.008 ms, below the detection floor
n16 had mis-attributed the producer: gM is 16 messages (2 instructions x 8 rows), 64 was the expand store.slm, and ord 193 does not write gY
append_after_L7.consequence: The global store->load layout-folding axis is closed as D unless a site lands on a kernel with a much larger isolated share. Mechanism knowledge is kept: the fold is expressible and provably exact, so it stays available for future shapes.

append_after_L7.claim: Per-lane operand reads are capped at 512 B per message; the wide opcodes are exec-1 broadcast block reads, so a shape or layout change cannot widen an operand read
evidence: n23 merged V0+V1 into one 8x32 accumulator reading a reblocked 12-file weight pack: gold frames matched byte-exactly, static instructions fell 4813->4705, yet load.ugm.d32x8.a32.bss[a0.2] stayed 96 and no d32x64t/d32x32t appeared

a read-only census over 2038 ISA captures shows d32x64t/d32x16t/d64x64t/d32x32t only ever appear at exec=1 with a uniform address and r4/r8 broadcast, while d32x8 a0.2 appears at exec16 rd:8 (= 16 lanes x 32 B = 512 B) 32767 times: no x16/x32/x64 form occurs at exec16/32 at all
arithmetic for the F05 C128 projection: 6 tiles x 8 k-steps x 2 phases x 512 B = 48 KB per SG per WG, and at 512 B per message the floor is 96 messages, which is exactly what the parent emits
the reblock n23 built is already contiguous column-major (element(k,n) = wq + h*12288 + p*4096 + ki*512 + n*16 + k), so "make the layout contiguous" was not a remaining lever
append_after_L7.consequence: Before claiming a message can be widened, check that the wider opcode ever occurs at exec16/32; if not, the only lever left is reading fewer bytes, which for F05 C128 means breaking the 2x row_phase duplication and paying 12 resident accumulators (96 GRF), measured at -0.349 ms (n05e). Treat 96 messages/WG as a proven lower bound for that pass.

append_after_L7.claim: Width scaling in F04 is quantitative, not qualitative: bytes per DPAS is constant across C64/C128/C256 and narrower widths do not free registers
evidence: n25 measured the three widths with one method (asserted against source-derived message and DPAS counts): bytes per DPAS 380.1 / 381.8 / 382.8, i.e. the same shape evaluated on a smaller K
max_r is 127 for all three widths and the data-side peak is also 127, so going narrower does not release registers (only one free GRF at C64)
the only qualitative difference is the arithmetic of the WG shape: cross-SG weight redundancy 256/C = 4x/2x/1x and mLocal multiplicity C/32 = 2x/4x/8x
C64s sync.allwr is 10 versus 37 (C128) and 70 (C256), so the sync axis is already the healthiest at the narrowest width
append_after_L7.consequence: Do not expect a different width to expose a new mechanism; measure the dominant cost share first (weights are 67.3% at C64) and check whether the proposed change touches it. Also do not offer registers as the lever for a cross-SG duplication problem: that constraint is shape, not count.

append_after_L7.claim: The F08 "bijective remap changed the frame" anomaly was not an order dependence: the dispatched plan still carried the parent grid, so the rotated index arithmetic ran on the unrotated launch grid
evidence: n26 proved the dispatched plan (sha fa2033aa…) differs from the baseline only in 16 SPV paths with grid still 66 2 1, while n08bs own plan (sha 98a26cfa…) had grid 4 33 1 and was never dispatched

the SPIR-V shows the axis really was swapped (component[1]x32 -> token, component[0]x2 -> group versus the parent component[0]x16, component[1]x4), and the ISA shows shr 2->shl 5 and shl 4->shl 1 on the same operands, so the shader change landed while the grid change did not
consequence measured: 132 workgroups with overlapping write domains, out-of-bounds weight reads, 29.6% of gf addresses written by the wrong workgroup and 0.4% never written

root cause was our own rebase helper silently dropping plan field edits; it was fixed (per-token field carrying) and unit-tested (doctored grid 169->338 lands on exactly one row) before the n23 shape card

quantified: gf writes 159744/540672 with 380928 (70.4%) never written, 143360 slots written more than once (up to 4 times), weights read to 8.65 MB against a 3.67 MB buffer; the first necessarily-different byte is 319488 and [0,16384) is guaranteed identical

end-to-end confirmation: re-running n08bs own plan (grid 4 33 1, sha 98a26cfa…) passes BOTH fixed and fb2 gates, while the same SPIR-V on 66 2 1 failed - the desync explanation is measured, not inferred
append_after_L7.consequence: Treat a "bijective remap changed the frame" claim as a plan/grid desync first: an indexing expression and the launch grid are two halves of one mapping and must be changed together. Also: any tool that rewrites plans must preserve non-SPV fields, or it will manufacture fake anomalies. n08 (grid 33 4 1, both gold frames pass) remains a valid -0.182 ms negative.

append_after_L7.claim: Hardware stall counters converted to milliseconds rank passes usefully within one run, but their aggregate percentages drift by ~5 points between runs and cannot resolve small effects
evidence: measured on the chain head: frame 17.142 ms of per-PASS GpuTime, of which 9.399 ms (54.8%) the XVE is not active; time-weighted stalls are ALUWR 3.670 ms (21.4%), SENDWR 2.161 ms (12.6%), PIPESTALL 1.680 ms (9.8%), BARRIER 1.433 ms (8.4%), PS_DEPENDENCY 0.292 ms (1.7%)

inter-dispatch gaps are only 17.524 - 17.142 = 0.382 ms (2.2%), so the 232 full pipeline barriers between dispatches are NOT where the serialisation money is - a persistent/tile-chain redesign is bounded by ~0.38 ms

the metric explains the campaign: n18 deleted a modulo chain that fed addresses (on the dependency path) for +0.079 ms, n19 deleted duplicate gathers off the path for +0.005 ms, and F20s four message-deleting cards were all null while its SENDWR is only 0.029 ms

message cost is position dependent: n05a paid 126 ps per deleted message where the message was serialised, while the frame average is 31 ps, so a linear message-price model over-predicts by 4x (a naive global application predicted 405% of the frame)

two runs of the same plan differed by ALUWR +3.79, SENDWR +4.58, BARRIER +4.56, PIPESTALL +4.42 and PS_DEPENDENCY +4.88 points while the deterministic XMX slot count was identical (9.8037e8) and the two largest kernels times were flat
append_after_L7.consequence: Use the counter budget to rank passes inside one run and to find big asymmetries. Do not read a difference of a few points across runs as an effect, and never let a counter delta override ordinary timing: the timing is the arbiter.

append_after_L7.claim: The AMD RDNA4 port of the same network has the same LDS-staging-plus-barrier structure; it hides the cost with double buffering and FP8 payloads rather than avoiding barriers
evidence: the AMD reference stages fragments in shared memory exactly as we do (ffwd3_t.comp: shared fe4m3vec4 lds_fr[...], lds_fh[2*...]; attn.comp: lds_q/lds_k/lds_v/lds_p) and its barrier counts are comparable (fswin_t.comp 27, fswin_body.glsl 16, attn.comp 13)
it double buffers with a [buf] dimension and hh / 1-hh index flipping, so the write of stage i+1 overlaps the read of stage i instead of waiting
its LDS payloads are NR_E4M3, so the same 16 KB holds twice the elements and the handoff needs half the transactions
its workgroups are smaller: 8x8 = 64 threads typical (2 waves) versus 205 of our 232 passes using 256 threads (8 subgroups), so its barriers fan in over 4x fewer waves
append_after_L7.consequence: Of the three AMD treatments only window rotation / barrier coalescing transfers without re-quantisation, and we have already proven it once (n10 merged two arenas and alternated the A-slice windows for +0.094 ms). Memory-doubling ping-pong is not free for us: F20 already uses 29184 B of workgroup memory, so doubling would cut resident workgroups (L4).

append_after_L7.claim: On this GPU the ALU operation class decides the payoff, not the count: two integer divisions bought +0.080 ms while 144 select instructions bought nothing
evidence: n29 removed two live modulo clusters from the F01 entry: math.inv 21->19, static instructions 6519->6403 (-116), dpas and max_r unchanged, gold byte-exact
the card had predicted under 0.02 ms from a 38-instruction estimate, because a plain instruction count prices a division like any other op
measured result +0.080363 ms CI[0.021442,0.139283], 6/6 pairs faster

the same kernel has 21 math.inv total; 19 of them sit in the arm that this fixture skips (ctl(8)=0 makes 1116 of 1351 entry instructions and 67 of 73 gathers not execute), which is why the remaining live chain is only 81 instructions

n31 deleted 144 sel instructions (the operand-swap identity, chain depth 155->142, independent chains 26->26 preserved) and measured -0.0396 ms CI[-0.1392,0.0600]: no gain, and the point estimate is if anything negative
append_after_L7.consequence: Price ALU work by operation class: integer division (math.inv) and square root (rsqt) at the top, casts in the middle, select/move/add at the bottom. A card that only removes cheap ops should not be opened. Also check the branch mask first: 21.4% of the post-0x4A90 region is skipped at debug==0.

append_after_L7.claim: Instruction-level parallelism is worth more than instruction count when it is lost at the same time as something else is gained; a drop in independent chains is a cost to weigh, not a veto
evidence: n28 removed one executed barrier (ISA sync.bar 12->11, the first real barrier deletion in the campaign) and cut mul 301->205 and add 944->851 by collapsing the tail from 4 independent FP32 chains per lane to 1: the frame got 0.1809 ms SLOWER CI[-0.3307,-0.0312], exactly the risk the card itself had written down (lane ILP 4->1)

n30 removed a different executed barrier (normal path 5->4, SPIR-V 16->15) with zero memory growth: the hardware counter showed XVE_STALL_BARRIER 16.109%->15.959%, i.e. 0.2173->0.2167 ms = -0.0006 ms, about 60x less than the predicted 0.037-0.045 ms
both cards passed both gold frames, so these are real landed changes, not implementation failures

n36 tier2 cut the QKV-section independent chains 6 -> 4 yet still measured +0.126122 ms, because the occupancy gain (2 -> 4 resident workgroups) dominated; so the earlier wording ("never collapse independent chains") was too strong
append_after_L7.consequence: Keep the rule "report chains before/after and treat a collapse as a cost", but do not refuse a card on chain count alone: n28 lost because it collapsed 4 chains to 1 with nothing gained, while n36 tier2 collapsed 6 to 4 and won 0.126 ms on occupancy.

append_after_L7.claim: The "exposed latency" census was an artefact of measuring the distance to the cast: by the correct index (distance to the first arithmetic consumer) the expensive ops were already hidden
evidence: the census counted, for every math.inv/math.rsqt, the distance to the first instruction reading the result; that first reader is usually the same-expression narrowing cast float16_t(...), so it is 1-2 regardless of the schedule (n33 measured parent [1]x16 and candidate [1]x16 in F02)

re-measured with d_arith (first mul/mad/add/fma reading the result): n32 parent pipe5 {28:4, 38:1, 40:1, 135:1, 197:1, 199:1} and pipe9 {25:4, 37:2, 129:1, 196:1, 198:1}, i.e. the arithmetic consumers were already 25-40 instructions away - more than enough to cover a ~20 cycle sqrt

the n32 candidate did change the schedule (distances scattered to 22..160) but there was nothing to hide, so both the measured frame effect (-0.0045 ms in the sibling F18 card) and the n32 verdict agree
n33 further showed that in F02 the source reorder cannot even change SPIR-V d_first, because the cast is part of the same expression
append_after_L7.consequence: Do not use cast-to-consumer distance as an exposure proxy. If a latency question ever comes up again, measure d_arith and compare against the operation latency before concluding that anything is exposed. This is the fifth time static text accounting overstated the machine (L11, L14, L18, L27, now L26).

append_after_L7.claim: Text-identical operands are not redundancy: a register name is reused across sites, and only a reaching-definition analysis can tell a duplicated computation from a reused register
evidence: a census that grouped math.inv/math.rsqt by their source operand text reported 173 redundant copies in 40 kernels (63% of the 275 expensive ops); n33 then ran a dword-granularity reaching-definition analysis on the F02 kernel and found the 24 ops there are 24 DISTINCT definitions, with at least one intervening write to the source dword between any two same-text sites and zero shared definitions
the same check on a0888c5a (F01, rsqt 10) and f3942341 (F19, rsqt 9) also returned zero genuine duplicates
only 575e6253 (F21) showed real redundancy: 12 copies of the same 1/x, exec-1 scalar, each block re-deriving it from the same mov
deleting a genuine-looking but non-redundant copy is E-class (the gold frames change), not A-class
append_after_L7.consequence: Before opening a redundancy card, prove all four: same reaching definition at dword granularity, no intervening write, same exec width, and consumers reading the same value. This is the fourth time static text accounting overstated the machine (see L11 lane masks, L14 fragment shapes, L18 source redundancy).

append_after_L7.claim: Genuine duplicated expensive ops are rare and already exhausted: the whole frame has only 26, and the only large group is the F18 case that was measured frame-null
evidence: applying the four-criteria test (bounded backward slice, identical leaf signature, same op, checks for intervening leaf writes) to all 40 kernels found exactly three groups: a606bc5d (F18 ord 166) 15 copies of 1/r2.4, 1ff52be5 (F17 ord 133) 11 copies of 1/r2.1, 05eea6a2 (F12 ord 92) 3 copies over r38.0

the F18 group is n35s candidate: the shared reciprocal landed as math.inv 16->1 and 1375->392 instructions (-71.5%) with both gold frames byte-exact, and measured -0.0045 ms CI[-0.0268, 0.0178], i.e. frame-null because that pass is 0.18% of the frame
the remaining two groups sit in families worth 0.2% of the frame each (F17 one pass, F12 two passes), so they cannot clear the detection floor by construction
the earlier text-matching census that claimed 173 duplicates was wrong for exactly the reason this test guards against: register names are reused
append_after_L7.consequence: Do not open further redundancy cards. The F18 candidate is kept as an asset: it is numerically exact and cuts 71.5% of that kernel, so it becomes valuable if the same pattern ever appears in a kernel with a larger frame share, or if F18 is ever repackaged.

append_after_L7.claim: Occupancy is capped by registers in every kernel and by shared memory above 16 KB; the only untried way to raise it is to shrink a workgroups working set, which is a shape change
evidence: a probe over the frame joined each PASSes measured occupancy/XVE activity with its own resources: 199 of 232 passes sit at max_r 127 and the remaining 33 report r255 (a special register), so effectively every kernel is at the 128-register ceiling
occupancy falls with shared memory above 16 KB: 8 KB -> 86.1%, 20 KB -> 81.7%, 24 KB -> 64.4%, 32 KB -> 41.7%
XVE activity does not follow occupancy monotonically (the 0 KB group has 79.9% occupancy but 32.0% activity, while 8 KB has 86.1% and 46.2%), so occupancy is necessary but not sufficient
the 17 passes at 32 KB are the clearest gap: 41.7% occupancy against 86.1% achieved elsewhere in the same frame

shrinking the staging buffer by segmenting it was already tried twice (n06c) and lost 0.0246 ms because it added staging messages and barriers; halving the tokens per workgroup (32 KB -> 16 KB, twice the workgroups) has NOT been tried and needs a paired grid change (L6)
append_after_L7.consequence: If occupancy is pursued, the concrete target is the 32 KB group: halve tokens per workgroup to reach ~16 KB and roughly double residency, with the SPIR-V and the launch grid changed together and a post-dispatch write-set proof that the coverage is unchanged.

append_after_L7.claim: Halving tokens per workgroup in the 32 KB kernel would raise occupancy 1.8x but costs +34.8% messages; a cheaper way to learn the occupancy slope is to make residency worse on purpose
evidence: 17 PASSes declare 32768 B of shared memory (F06 15 + F18 2) with 2189 workgroups per frame; their measured occupancy is 41.7% against 86.1% for the 8 KB group in the same frame

the kernel message mix per thread is load.slm.d32x8t 1024 (staging reads, proportional to tokens) plus per-workgroup traffic: load.ugm.d32x8 256 (weights), load.ugm.d32x8t 128, store.ugm.d32x8t 128, store.ugm.d32x64t 16 and small items
scaling that mix to half the tokens per workgroup (twice the workgroups) leaves staging totals unchanged but doubles everything per-workgroup: total messages 3.50e6 -> 4.71e6 per frame, +34.8%

the uncertainty is genuine: this same kernel was shown insensitive to message count when n06d cut its messages 54% and the frame did not move (-0.0025 ms), while its occupancy gap is the largest in the frame
append_after_L7.consequence: Before rewriting the kernel shape, measure the slope the cheap way: pad the shared array so residency halves with zero change to the maths, and see how much the frame slows. That gives the occupancy elasticity from one GPU slot without touching the index arithmetic.

append_after_L7.claim: Residency is the one lever with a measured large elasticity: halving it on the 32 KB group costs 0.364 ms, more than half of that group whole frame time
evidence: a reverse probe padded the F06 C256 staging array from 32768 B to 49152 B with zero change to the maths (parent reproduced byte-exactly, both gold frames still exact), so the SM could host one workgroup instead of two
the frame got -0.363969 ms SLOWER CI[-0.587234, -0.140704], 6/6 pairs, on a group that only sums to about 0.56 ms of GPU time
the same frame contains a 16 KB group at 75.7% occupancy against 41.7% for the 32 KB group, so the opposite direction is physically available
the message cost of getting there is +34.8% by the arithmetic in L30, and this same kernel was previously shown insensitive to a 54% message cut (n06d, -0.0025 ms)
append_after_L7.consequence: The next card should halve the tokens per workgroup in the 32 KB group (32768 -> 16384, twice the workgroups), with the SPIR-V and the launch grid changed together and a post-dispatch write-set proof. This is the only remaining lever with a measured upside of order 0.2-0.3 ms.

append_after_L7.claim: Residency is the dominant lever in this frame: halving it on F05 costs 1.219 ms, 40% of the familys own GPU time and far more than any optimisation adopted so far
evidence: the same reverse-probe method was applied to F05 (36 PASS, shared qkv 24576 B): pad to 49152 B with zero maths change, all three shader groups reproduced byte-exactly first, both gold frames still exact
the frame got -1.218946 ms SLOWER CI[-1.237396, -1.200497], 6/6 pairs, while F05 sums to about 3.04 ms of GPU time
the earlier probe on the 32 KB F06 group gave -0.364 ms for the same 2->1 residency change, so the effect scales with how much frame time the group owns
the frame contains groups at 95.8% occupancy, so headroom exists in principle for every group below that
append_after_L7.consequence: Freeing shared memory per workgroup is now the top-ranked lever: for F05 the concrete moves are (a) overlap the Q/K/V phases in one arena the way n10 merged two arenas, taking 24576 B to 16384 B without changing the token tile, or (b) halve the token tile per workgroup, which needs a paired grid change. Try (a) first because it needs no grid change.

append_after_L7.claim: The two occupancy probes bracket the SM shared-memory pool at [65536, 73728) bytes, which turns residency into arithmetic instead of guesswork
evidence: F05 probe: 24576 B gave 2 resident workgroups, 49152 B gave 1, so the pool is at least 49152 and below 98304
F06 probe: 32768 B gave 2, 49152 B gave 1, so the pool is at least 65536 and below 98304
combining: the pool lies in [65536, 73728), because 24576 x 3 = 73728 is the first value that would have given F05 three workgroups
at both ends of that interval floor(P/24576) = 2 and floor(P/16384) = 4, so shrinking the F05 arena from 24576 to 16384 B is a 2 -> 4 residency move regardless of the exact pool size
append_after_L7.consequence: Residency targets follow from the declared shared-memory size alone: the thresholds are about 32768 (2 workgroups), 21845 (3), 16384 (4), 13107 (5) bytes. A card that wants more residency should aim just below the next threshold, not at an arbitrary smaller number.

append_after_L7.claim: The standard verification gates are blind to a wrong address literal, and a plan does not pin the candidate bytes it dispatches
evidence: the first n36 candidate passed storage-byte accounting, spv_validate, parent-byte reproduction, the coopmat and NoContraction multisets and the hazard model, yet failed the fixed gold frame: one plane-base literal +4096u inside the V section had not been updated when the section stride changed 6144 -> 4096, so the PV read went out of the section
the hazard and offset models used the intended offsets, not the literal in the source text, which is why they were all silent

the fix (16 sites, 4096u -> 0u) left the plan file unchanged, because the plan stores SPV paths and not their hashes: the plan sha stayed 21292385 while the candidate sha changed to 236aad96, so dispatch identity must be checked by SPV sha
the dedicated gate that caught it strips the section base and checks each access literal against the allowed set and the section bounds (_addr_audit.py in the n36 card)
append_after_L7.consequence: Any card that changes an arena stride or plane layout must run an address-literal audit in addition to the usual gates, and must record the SPV hashes it dispatches rather than the plan hash.

append_after_L7.claim: The plans shared-memory field is stale for 18 of 232 rows; the module declaration is the only authority
evidence: recomputed every PASSes workgroup memory from its SPIR-V (sum of Workgroup-storage variables) and compared with the plans field: 18 rows disagree
F09 (16 rows) declares 16384 B in the plan but its modules declare 0 B: n09b deleted the sx staging and the field was never updated
F18 body (ord 193) plan 32768 vs true 16384, and F20 (ord 230) plan 29184 vs true 24576 (n38 found the latter: the field still counted the deleted P publish region)

the occupancy ranking that motivated the n36/n37/n38 cards was built from the plan field, so its group labels were partly wrong even though the top targets (F05 24576, F06 32768, F10 20480) were right
append_after_L7.consequence: Read the workgroup-memory size from the SPIR-V, never from the plan. Residency arithmetic (floor(P/W) with P in [65536,73728)) must use the declared size.

append_after_L7.claim: A declared shared-memory size can be larger than the simultaneous live peak; the difference is structural slack that a retire window can reclaim
evidence: n37 measured F10: the declared 20480 B exceeds the live peak 16384 B, and the extra 4096 B comes from the alternation of the staging window with the handoff region (8192 + 12288), not from live data
the reclaim is one 8192 B window (W0, empty after the handoff) handed to Q+K with V moved into the first 2048 halves of W1, costing exactly one workgroup barrier for a 4096 B WAR edge
n27 earlier cut the same kind of slack on F06 C256 by making the staging rows contiguous, and n36 cut F05 from 24576 to 16384 by moving a producer
on this GPU the cost of one barrier is small: n30 deleted one real barrier in F20 and the frame moved by -0.0006 ms, inside the counter noise
append_after_L7.consequence: When a kernel declares more shared memory than its live peak, look for the slack before redesigning anything: reclaiming it moves the workgroup up an occupancy threshold (thresholds: 32768 / 21845 / 16384 / 13107 B) and usually costs one barrier rather than a rewrite.

append_after_L7.claim: Residency elasticity is not a constant: the same kind of shared-memory cut paid on F05 (36 passes) and paid nothing on F20 (1 pass)
evidence: F05: shrink the arena 24576 -> 16384 B (33%), residency 2 -> 4, measured +0.116668 and +0.126122 ms on the two tiers
F20: retire shY into shX, 24576 -> 20480 B (17%), residency 2 -> 3, measured +0.000503 ms CI[-0.0103, +0.0113]
both candidates landed exactly (gold byte-exact, no new barriers in F20, no new messages) so the difference is not implementation quality
the likely reason is saturation: F20 has 16393 workgroups in a single dispatch and already fills the machine at two resident workgroups, while F05 is 36 dispatches sharing the same limit
append_after_L7.consequence: Before spending effort on a shared-memory cut for a family, check how many workgroups it launches and how much GPU time it owns; an occupancy gap in the counter is not by itself a promise of a frame-level gain.

append_after_L7.claim: Residency is causal but pays unevenly: it responded on F05 (short kernels) and not on F10 or F20 (long kernels)
evidence: control: padding the adopted F05 arena back to 24576 B while keeping its restructured code costs -0.369730 ms CI[-0.384386, -0.355074], 6/6, so the earlier +0.117 and +0.126 ms came from residency and not from the V-projection move
F10 shrank 20480 -> 16384 B (residency 3 -> 4) and measured +0.008909 ms CI[-0.0186, +0.0364]: not significant
F20 shrank 24576 -> 20480 B (residency 2 -> 3) and measured +0.000503 ms CI[-0.0103, +0.0113]: flat
the three differ in kernel length: F05 is 36 short dispatches (about 0.08 ms each) sharing the same limit, F10 is 16 dispatches of about 0.13 ms, F20 is one 1.36 ms dispatch with 16393 workgroups
the control also shows the curve is concave: giving up residency costs 0.370 ms while gaining it paid 0.243 ms
append_after_L7.consequence: Target residency work at families made of many short dispatches, where wave drain is a large share of the time. For a long single dispatch the machine is already saturated and cutting shared memory buys nothing. Always pair such a card with its own pad-back control before claiming the mechanism.

append_after_L7.claim: A landing proof and a causal proof are different things: deleting a buffer is provable from native and declarations, but which of the simultaneous effects paid is not
evidence: n39 removed a 32 KiB identity copy, its publish barrier and its fence, and pointed the A operand at global memory; it won +0.103768 ms in a balanced batch
all of that is provable from the ISA and the SPIR-V, yet three separate things changed at once: the copy disappeared, the feed path changed from SLM to global reads, and workgroup memory fell to zero

nothing in the measurement separates those three; asserting "the new global reads hit L2" or "residency rose to at least 4" would be inference from tile size and from one removed constraint, not measurement
max_r staying at 127 similarly says nothing about GRF allocation, achieved residency or spills
append_after_L7.consequence: In every card, split the attribution into (a) what native and declarations prove, (b) what timing proves, and (c) what is not established. Only claim (a) and (b). A reverse probe on the same family is the cheapest way to upgrade (c).

lessons.claim: Source-level address-recompute folding does not reduce work on this toolchain
evidence: n09-f09-f11-store (F11): SPIR-V body 449->291, OpFunctionCall 18->2, but ISA add 254->284, mul 88->88, IC 998->998, +6 sync; ordinary -0.0011ms INDISTINCT
n04a-f05-c64-feed (F05 C64): SPIR-V -93 integer ops, but ISA add 810->810, mul 242->242, only shl -16/sync -16, allwr +7, first DPAS +168B; ordinary -0.098ms SLOWER_95
lessons.consequence: Do not open a card whose only mechanism is removing address arithmetic. IGC either already emits base+imm or re-expands the folded form, and the re-scheduling can cost more than the deleted ops.
lessons.counterexample_note: n04b measured that F05 C128 A row addresses are already base+imm in ISA, so there is nothing to fold there by construction.

lessons.claim: What actually pays is deleting duplicated memory messages while keeping the same occupancy
evidence: n05a-f05-c256-mreuse: 96 duplicated same-address weight tiles removed (load.ugm.d32x8 200->104, send 1014->917), DPAS/sync-gold unchanged, max_r unchanged -> +0.521ms FASTER_95
n06-f06-output: weight pair shared across two M blocks (send 481->449, mul 105->73) -> +0.040ms, CI lower bound +0.0012ms (fragile)
lessons.consequence: Prefer candidates whose native signature is a message-count drop at constant register pressure. Static instruction drops alone have not produced a measurable frame delta at 8-16 PASS scope.

lessons.claim: Static instruction reduction in an 8-16 PASS kernel is below the frame-level detection floor, even when it is large
evidence: n03-f04-middle: -620 instructions, send -32, mov -337 -> -0.023ms INDISTINCT
n11-vit-ffn: -2290 instructions, mov -1771, jmpi -129 -> +0.039ms INDISTINCT
n12-vit-qkv: goto/join 20->0, indirect reads 8->0 -> -0.007ms INDISTINCT
n07n14-arena: -412 instructions, send -52 -> -0.030ms INDISTINCT
lessons.consequence: Single-kernel wins of this size must be packaged (same mechanism over more PASSes) before they can be judged; a single INDISTINCT is not evidence that the removed work was worthless.

lessons.claim: Increasing per-workgroup or per-subgroup live values loses more than the saved exchange
evidence: n08-f08-wg-map: weight footprint per WG halved (512->256 KiB) but input footprint doubled (16->32 KiB) and dispatch y 2->4 -> -0.182ms SLOWER_95
n13-vit-attn: send -294, static -888, but each SG now holds two query fragments and mul +70 -> -0.113ms SLOWER_95
lessons.consequence: Any candidate that raises live registers or per-owner resident data needs a budget first (n04b measured ~107/128 GRF at 6 accumulators for F05 C128).

lessons.claim: Identity A copies are already free in F02; narrowing is the irreducible rounding point
evidence: n01-c32-chain: 20 identity A-copy sites deleted, ISA +149 instructions of which +160 = 20x8 came from re-narrowing in the debug path; by net arithmetic the 20 identity copies were worth ~11 instructions total (0.55/instruction site)
n01 also showed K/V cross-SG handoffs were already store-in-consumer-layout, and per-element half copies in native are almost absent (11 mov.hf)
lessons.consequence: Do not price a handoff by its source-level statement count; measure one narrowing (8 instructions) and one copy (~0.55) and use those units.

lessons.claim: A bijective workgroup remap changed the fixed frame in F08, which is unexplained and must be resolved before any F08 dispatch-order experiment
evidence: n08b-f08-order: only two WGID swaps + grid (33,4)->(4,33); coverage is a bijection; fixed frame 443559e8 != gold 1755e9c2, nan/inf 0, 232 passes, normal close
lessons.consequence: Treat as an implementation/identity problem (triage E). Do not use the failure as evidence about dispatch order, and do not build further F08 order cards until the WG-order dependence is located.

lessons.claim: Compiler-time branches decide what is in the module; read the recipe before claiming a store/tail is already optimal
evidence: n09 found F11 is built with -DKIND=1, so the half_tail repack branch is not in the module at all; idt confirmed -DKIND=1/2/3 for F11/F12 and -DPROJECT_PAIR=2 for F17
lessons.consequence: Always reproduce the parent bytes from its recorded recipe (evidence/RECIPES.json, 39/39 verified) before reasoning about source-level branches.
